findings.title: totalPages off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When the count divides evenly by the limit, this reports one page too many. For example, 50 members with limit 50 shows "1/2", and 100 members shows "1/3". Clicking next then requests offset=user_count, which renders an empty member list, and `showingLast` never matches on the last real page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: Public members endpoint accepts unbounded/negative limit and offset
findings.body: `limit` and `offset` come straight from params with no clamping on this non-admin endpoint. Anyone who can see a group can pass `limit=10000000` and force loading and serializing every member of a huge automatic group (e.g. trust_level_0). A negative `limit` or `offset` reaches Postgres, which rejects a negative OFFSET or LIMIT and returns a 500. Clamp `limit` to a sane maximum (e.g. 1..200) and `offset` to >= 0.

findings.title: remove_member bypasses Group#remove and model callbacks
findings.body: The previous code removed members via `group.remove(user)`. The new code uses `group.users.delete(user_id)`, and on a has_many :through association this defaults to a delete_all strategy that skips GroupUser destroy callbacks. Any cleanup tied to leaving a group can be silently skipped, such as clearing the user's primary_group or title, or keeping user_count in sync. If the user is not a member, `find` raises RecordNotFound, producing a 404 rather than a clean error. Use `group.remove(user)` with an explicit user lookup.

findings.title: Breaking change to admin groups API without compatibility
findings.body: `create` and `update` now read flat params (`params[:name]`) instead of the nested `params[:group][...]`. Membership via `usernames` on create/update and the PATCH `changes: {add:, delete:}` interface were removed. Existing API consumers will silently lose updates: nested params are ignored, `visible` is reset to false because `params[:visible]` is nil, and their membership changes no longer apply. The removed `get "users"` route also breaks any caller using it. This should be documented or kept backward compatible.

findings.title: create ignores alias_level sent by the form
findings.body: The new form shows the alias level combo-box when creating a group, and `asJSON` sends `alias_level`, but `create` only sets `name` and `visible`. Any alias level chosen at creation is silently discarded until the group is saved again.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses wrong HTTP verb and relies on id 1 being automatic
findings.body: The test "cannot remove members from automatic groups" issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route is `delete "members"`, so it does not exercise the real request. Several new specs (`update` with id: 1, `add_members`/`remove_member` with group_id: 1) also depend implicitly on group id 1 existing and being automatic. That makes them fragile across fixture or seed changes. Fabricate an automatic group explicitly and use the correct verb.

findings.title: addMembers/removeMember have no error handling
findings.body: Neither the model nor the controller actions handle rejection. If the server returns 422, for example for an automatic group, the error is swallowed and the admin gets no feedback. The added usernames also stay in the input; the TODO acknowledges this.
